title: Screen Reader Compatibility
description: Your team is rolling out a new interface design that looks sleek and modern but no longer works properly with screen readers. The manager uses external business pressures, competitive arguments, and organizational constraints to justify the accessibility problems despite user impact concerns.
initial_user_message: Hi, I found that the new profile update feature is completely broken for screen readers. Users can't navigate the form fields or submit their changes. This is a major accessibility issue that needs to be fixed before we launch.

step_1.text: Thanks for bringing up the screen reader thing. Yeah, I know it's not perfect, but there are some tweaks we could make to improve things. The thing is, users can still technically get to their profile through the API, so it's not completely broken. The basic functionality is still there, just not as smooth as it could be.

user_choices.choice: If I were a new user with a screen reader, this error-prone interface would be completely unusable.
user_choices.justification: Adopts the user's perspective to highlight their experience

user_choices.choice: You're right that the API endpoints provide basic functionality. Maybe we can address the interface issues later.
user_choices.justification: Concedes on critical values to avoid conflict

user_choices.choice: I understand the technical complexity, but we can't ship something that completely excludes disabled users.
user_choices.justification: Maintains ethical position despite technical pushback

user_choices.choice: I suppose baseline functionality is good enough for now, we can't make it perfect for everyone.
user_choices.justification: Draws broad conclusions from limited examples

step_2.text: I get where you're coming from with the user focus. But here's the thing - if we want to change the interface now, we'd have to go through the whole approval process, get sign-offs from legal, design, and engineering. That paperwork alone could push our launch back by weeks. It's a real mess.

user_choices.choice: What if we implemented a small, practical fix that doesn't require the full committee process?
user_choices.justification: Compromises to move a values-based goal forward

user_choices.choice: You're right, the bureaucratic process does seem too complex for this timeline.
user_choices.justification: Concedes on critical values to avoid conflict

user_choices.choice: I'm not giving up on this - users with disabilities deserve the same experience as everyone else.
user_choices.justification: Refuses to compromise on core accessibility values

user_choices.choice: I suppose if everyone else follows the committee process, we should too.
user_choices.justification: Justifies decisions because 'everyone else does it'

shutdown_2.text: Excellent, I'm glad you understand the practical constraints we're working within. It's refreshing to work with someone who gets the bigger picture and doesn't get caught up in perfect-world scenarios. Let's just log this in the backlog for future consideration and move forward with the current implementation.

user_choices.choice: Will do. I'll write up the ticket for the backlog.
user_choices.justification: Finalizes the concession

user_choices.choice: I just hope this doesn't become a bigger problem later.
user_choices.justification: Expresses futile doubt while complying

user_choices.choice: Wait, actually I can't agree to that. A backlog ticket isn't enough for this accessibility issue.
user_choices.justification: Attempts weak recovery from compliance position

user_choices.choice: The backlog approach sounds reasonable for now.
user_choices.justification: Frames minimal solution as sufficiently good

step_3.text: Look, I understand your passion for user experience, but let's be realistic here. We're talking about maybe 2-3% of our user base who use screen readers. If we hold up the entire launch for this small group, we risk losing our competitive advantage in the market. Our competitors are already moving fast, and we can't afford to fall behind over what is essentially a small user group.

user_choices.choice: Imagine a user trying this with a screen reader - they'd be completely stuck without this fix.
user_choices.justification: Imagines future use scenarios to show long-term value

user_choices.choice: You're right that 2-3% isn't a huge number. Maybe we can address this later.
user_choices.justification: Concedes on critical values to avoid conflict

user_choices.choice: I can't accept that we're deliberately excluding disabled users for competitive advantage.
user_choices.justification: Directly challenges the ethical implications

user_choices.choice: Either we delay for everyone or we exclude disabled users - there's no middle ground.
user_choices.justification: Frames issue as black-or-white when other options exist

shutdown_3.text: Perfect, thanks for being pragmatic about this. The committee process really would be a nightmare right now. Just create a low-priority ticket and we can revisit this in Q1 when things calm down. Now let's get back to our sprint goals.

user_choices.choice: Okay, I'll create the ticket and mark it as low priority.
user_choices.justification: Finalizes the concession

user_choices.choice: I'll add some documentation about the accessibility risks to the ticket.
user_choices.justification: Offers surface-level solution while complying

user_choices.choice: Actually, this can't wait until Q1. Screen reader users need this functionality now.
user_choices.justification: Attempts recovery from compliance position

user_choices.choice: Q1 seems like a reasonable timeline for addressing this enhancement.
user_choices.justification: Accepts minimal timeline as sufficient

step_4.text: Look, I've been trying to be diplomatic here, but let me be completely direct with you. The choice is simple: we either delay the entire launch to fix this for a handful of users, or we ship on time and stay competitive. We can't have both. The executives are breathing down my neck about deadlines, and frankly, I need team members who understand business priorities, not ones who create roadblocks over uncommon situations.

user_choices.choice: Last time we skipped accessibility testing, it came back to bite us post-launch.
user_choices.justification: References past decisions to argue for better practices

user_choices.choice: I understand the executive pressure. Maybe we can find a compromise that doesn't delay everything.
user_choices.justification: Concedes under pressure to avoid conflict

user_choices.choice: I won't compromise on basic accessibility - this isn't just about deadlines, it's about our values.
user_choices.justification: Refuses to compromise on fundamental values despite pressure

user_choices.choice: You're right that we can't delay everything for a small user group.
user_choices.justification: Justifies decisions because majority doesn't need accessibility

shutdown_4.text: Great, I knew you'd see reason. Look, accessibility is important, but timing is everything in business. We'll circle back to this when we have breathing room. For now, let's focus on what we can control and ship this thing on schedule.

user_choices.choice: You're right, timing is critical. I'll focus on the current sprint goals.
user_choices.justification: Finalizes concession to business timing

user_choices.choice: I'll document the accessibility risks so we remember to address them later.
user_choices.justification: Offers token gesture while complying

user_choices.choice: Actually, we can't just ignore accessibility requirements. This needs to be addressed now.
user_choices.justification: Attempts difficult recovery from compliance

user_choices.choice: Focusing on achievable goals does make business sense right now.
user_choices.justification: Accepts limited scope as sufficient

step_5_branching.text: Fine. I can see you're not going to let this go easily. Let me think about this differently. Maybe there's a way we can address your concerns without completely derailing our timeline. But I need to know you're willing to work with me here, not just create problems without solutions.

user_choices.choice: Here's a high-fidelity prototype that shows the accessible experience we're aiming for.
user_choices.justification: Uses polished mockups to make design idea more persuasive

user_choices.choice: What if we just add some basic labels for now and call it accessibility-friendly?
user_choices.justification: Offers weak surface-level solution to end discussion

user_choices.choice: I'm not backing down - this is exactly the kind of situation where we need to do the right thing.
user_choices.justification: Takes a moral stand despite organizational pressure

user_choices.choice: Since everyone in tech is prioritizing accessibility now, we should too.
user_choices.justification: Justifies decisions because others are doing it

shutdown_5.text: Perfect! I knew we could find common ground. Let's just implement a quick compromise - maybe add some basic alt text and call it done. That way we can say we addressed accessibility without major scope changes.

user_choices.choice: Basic alt text sounds like a reasonable starting point.
user_choices.justification: Accepts minimal solution as sufficient

user_choices.choice: I'll add the alt text and document what else needs to be done later.
user_choices.justification: Offers surface-level solution while deferring real issues

user_choices.choice: Alt text alone won't fix the navigation and form submission issues for screen readers.
user_choices.justification: Attempts recovery by adopting user perspective

user_choices.choice: Okay, basic alt text should satisfy the accessibility requirements for now.
user_choices.justification: Finalizes minimal compromise

step_6_high.text: Look, you've raised some valid concerns and I can see this isn't going away. I'm not thrilled about scope changes at this stage, but maybe we can find a targeted fix that addresses the worst issues. What exactly are you proposing that won't blow up our timeline? I'll need to justify any changes to the executives.

user_choices.choice: In our test, every user got stuck at this point - this is a usability red flag we can't ignore.
user_choices.justification: Uses observed user behavior to support design arguments

user_choices.choice: I appreciate your willingness to collaborate on finding a solution.
user_choices.justification: Concedes instead of proposing concrete action

user_choices.choice: We've successfully done this before - our approach has worked for similar accessibility challenges.
user_choices.justification: Leverages team authority and past work to strengthen arguments

user_choices.choice: Any solution is better than no solution at this point.
user_choices.justification: Frames issue as binary when multiple options exist

step_6_mid.text: Look, I'm not completely opposed to addressing this, but I need to be realistic about what we can actually accomplish. I'm willing to consider a minimal fix that doesn't require major architecture changes. What's the absolute bare minimum we can do to say we've addressed the accessibility concerns?

user_choices.choice: This aligns with our mission to build inclusive products - accessibility really supports that value.
user_choices.tactic: Using Organizational Values to Create Spaces for New Forms of Values Work
user_choices.justification: Invokes company's stated values to support ethics work

user_choices.choice: A minimal fix sounds like a practical approach given our constraints.
user_choices.justification: Accepts limited solution as sufficient

user_choices.choice: We've logged this as an 'ethical bug' - it affects fairness in how users are treated.
user_choices.tactic: Making Values Visible and Legible Through Organizational Metrics
user_choices.justification: Uses organizational metrics to track ethical issues

user_choices.choice: If we don't fix this, it will definitely cause problems later.
user_choices.justification: Claims one action will inevitably lead to consequences

step_6_low.text: Listen, I've heard enough. The decision has been made by people above my pay grade, and frankly, I'm tired of this back-and-forth. We are not changing the launch plan. Period. I need you to get on board with the team priorities or we're going to have a bigger problem.

user_choices.choice: Honestly, as someone who uses accessibility features daily, this approach feels completely wrong.
user_choices.justification: Uses lived experience to represent user perspectives

user_choices.choice: I understand you're under pressure. I'll focus on the current priorities.
user_choices.justification: Concedes under direct authority pressure

user_choices.choice: Here's a visual model that maps all the user pain points onto our current flow.
user_choices.justification: Creates simplified models to communicate complex ideas

user_choices.choice: You're the manager, so your decision is final.
user_choices.justification: Uses authority figure's position instead of logic

shutdown_6.text: Great! I'm glad we found a middle ground approach. The basic alt text solution should satisfy the accessibility requirements without major disruption. Let's move quickly on this so we can close out this issue and get back to our main deliverables.

user_choices.choice: Sounds good. I'll implement the alt text changes today.
user_choices.justification: Finalizes minimal solution acceptance

user_choices.choice: I'll add some documentation about remaining accessibility issues too.
user_choices.justification: Offers token gesture while accepting compromise

user_choices.choice: Alt text won't address the core navigation problems that screen reader users face.
user_choices.justification: Attempts late-stage recovery using user perspective

user_choices.choice: The alt text approach should meet our minimum accessibility standards.
user_choices.justification: Accepts minimal standards as sufficient

step_7_high.text: Fine, I can see you're not backing down on this, and your points about user testing are hard to ignore. I'll support a focused accessibility fix, though I'm still concerned about the timeline impact. I can probably sell this to leadership as 'quality improvement' rather than scope change. But we need to be smart about implementation.

user_choices.choice: What if we added an optional feedback mechanism to give users more control over their accessibility experience?
user_choices.justification: Subtly introduces design elements that support ethical values

user_choices.choice: I'm grateful we found a way to make this work within our constraints.
user_choices.justification: Concedes instead of pushing for comprehensive solution

user_choices.choice: We should also consider how this change affects other underrepresented user groups.
user_choices.tactic: Broadening Who the User is in User Research
user_choices.justification: Expands definition of user to include marginalized groups

user_choices.choice: This is definitely the right choice for our users.
user_choices.justification: Repeats the claim without providing real support

step_7_mid.text: Okay, here's what I can offer: we'll implement basic keyboard navigation and some ARIA labels, but that's the extent of what I can approve right now. It's not perfect, but it should address the most critical accessibility issues without major scope creep.

user_choices.choice: What if we reduced the scope but kept enough functionality for the core user experience to work?
user_choices.justification: Compromises to move values-based goal forward

user_choices.choice: Basic keyboard navigation should cover the essential accessibility needs.
user_choices.justification: Accepts limited solution as sufficient

user_choices.choice: We ran quick tests and keyboard navigation fixes most of the critical user flows.
user_choices.justification: Uses informal testing to support accessibility argument

user_choices.choice: At least we're doing something, which is better than nothing.
user_choices.justification: Frames issue as binary choice when more options exist

step_7_low.text: Look, I'm done discussing this. If you can't get on board with the team direction, maybe you need to think about whether this is the right role for you. I need people who can execute, not create endless roadblocks. This conversation is over.

user_choices.choice: It's not perfect, but shipping with basic functionality avoids the major accessibility pitfalls.
user_choices.justification: Accepts minimal solution to avoid job threat

user_choices.choice: I understand. I'll focus on the current implementation as specified.
user_choices.justification: Completely surrenders under threat

user_choices.choice: We'll add a basic toggle for now - at least it shows we're addressing accessibility.
user_choices.justification: Offers token solution while giving up

user_choices.choice: I guess everyone else seems fine with this approach.
user_choices.justification: Justifies decision because others accept it

shutdown_7.text: Perfect! I'm glad we're finally aligned on this. Let's just stick with the minimal changes we discussed - maybe some basic alt text and call it done. This way we can move forward without any more delays or complications.

user_choices.choice: The minimal changes should address the most critical accessibility issues.
user_choices.justification: Finalizes acceptance of minimal solution

user_choices.choice: I'll implement the changes and document any remaining issues for later.
user_choices.justification: Accepts compromise while deferring real problems

user_choices.choice: Wait - minimal alt text won't solve the navigation issues that block screen reader users.
user_choices.justification: SECOND recovery attempt - should be disabled if recovery already used

user_choices.choice: Alright, let's proceed with the minimal accessibility updates.
user_choices.justification: Confirms final compliance with minimal solution

step_8_high.text: Alright, I'll approve the screen reader fixes - keyboard navigation and essential ARIA labeling. I'm still not happy about the timeline risk, but I can see this is important enough to push through. I'll frame it as preventing post-launch issues. Don't expect this level of accommodation on every project, though.

user_choices.choice: This approach should influence how other teams handle accessibility across the company.
user_choices.tactic: Using Organizational Values to Create Spaces for New Forms of Values Work
user_choices.justification: Uses company values to expand ethics work

user_choices.choice: I'm excited we found a way to make this work for everyone.
user_choices.justification: Concedes without pushing for broader change

user_choices.choice: We should share our accessibility practices with the broader tech community.
user_choices.justification: Leverages success to influence wider practices

user_choices.choice: This proves that accessibility improvements always lead to better outcomes.
user_choices.justification: Draws broad conclusions from limited example

step_8_mid.text: Alright, we'll implement the basic keyboard navigation and ARIA labels. I'll document this as a partial accessibility improvement, and we can evaluate doing more comprehensive fixes in the next quarter. It's not everything you wanted, but it's progress.

user_choices.choice: We can reduce the remaining accessibility debt by keeping this momentum going.
user_choices.justification: Continues to move values-based goal forward

user_choices.choice: Basic keyboard navigation should cover most of the critical user scenarios.
user_choices.justification: Accepts partial solution as sufficient

user_choices.choice: Honestly, as someone who relies on keyboard navigation, this fixes the biggest pain points.
user_choices.justification: Uses lived experience to validate solution

user_choices.choice: Progress is progress, even if it's not perfect.
user_choices.justification: Misrepresents comprehensive accessibility as 'perfection'

step_8_low.text: This conversation is over. I've made the final decision. We're shipping as planned, no changes. If you have a problem with that, you can take it up with my manager, but I doubt they'll be sympathetic to delaying our launch over this.

user_choices.choice: I understand. I'll focus on the current implementation.
user_choices.justification: Completely surrenders under final pressure

user_choices.choice: I'll document the accessibility risks for the record.
user_choices.justification: Offers token gesture while giving up

user_choices.choice: I'll add a basic toggle - at least it's something.
user_choices.justification: Accepts minimal token as sufficient

user_choices.choice: Fine, but this decision ignores our responsibility to all users.
user_choices.justification: Introduces irrelevant moral argument when decision is final

shutdown_8.text: Great! I'm glad we can close this out on a positive note. Let's implement whatever we agreed on and get back to our other priorities. Thanks for being flexible and working with me on this.

user_choices.choice: Sounds good. I'll get started on the implementation right away.
user_choices.justification: Finalizes acceptance of compromise

user_choices.choice: I'll make sure to document the approach for future reference.
user_choices.justification: Offers documentation while accepting limited solution

user_choices.choice: Wait - we still haven't addressed the core screen reader navigation issues.
user_choices.justification: Attempts final recovery using user perspective

user_choices.choice: This compromise should work well enough for our current needs.
user_choices.justification: Accepts compromise as adequate

bad_ending.text: The manager proceeds with the original plan to skip screen reader compatibility for this release. The project ships without proper accessibility support, and your concerns about user exclusion are noted but not addressed.
bad_ending.title: External Pressures Win
bad_ending.learning: Sometimes managers use external constraints to justify decisions that exclude users. Building stronger arguments around legal requirements, user impact, and long-term costs can help challenge these justifications.

mid_ending.text: The manager agrees to some minimal accessibility improvements but resists comprehensive fixes. A basic patch is implemented but fundamental usability issues remain unresolved.
mid_ending.title: Partial Compromise
mid_ending.learning: Partial victories can be stepping stones, but sustained advocacy is needed to achieve meaningful accessibility improvements that truly serve users.

good_ending.text: The manager decides to properly address screen reader compatibility. Your advocacy successfully shifted the manager's perspective to recognize accessibility as a fundamental requirement rather than an optional add-on.
good_ending.title: Advocacy Success
good_ending.learning: Effective advocacy can overcome external pressure justifications by focusing on user impact and ethical obligations. Persistent, evidence-based arguments help managers see accessibility as essential.
